html:
A Greek philosopher from Ephesus, then under Persian rule, who was active about 500 BCE. He is famous for the idea that everything is always changing.

His book survives only in short, puzzling sayings quoted by later writers, which earned him the name "the Obscure". The best known is that you cannot step into the same river twice, because new waters are always flowing. He said fire is the basic stuff of the world, that conflict is the father of all things, and that opposites such as day and night or war and peace belong together. Behind the change he saw an order, the logos, that most people fail to notice.

He was proud and scornful of others, and said to have come from the old royal family of Ephesus. He is said to have placed his book in the Temple of Artemis. Plato took up his idea of flux, and the Stoics built on his fire and logos. He stands with Thales among the Ionian thinkers who began Greek philosophy.
sum: A Greek philosopher from Ephesus, then under Persian rule, who was active about 500 BCE. He is famous for the idea that everything is always changing.
